parsed.study_design: Cross-sectional household questionnaire survey with life-cycle cost analysis
parsed.population_and_sample: 315 households in five sub-districts of Metro City, Lampung, surveyed in October 2020
parsed.exposure: Household water-service arrangement and financing model, particularly self-supplied boreholes or dug wells versus public piped water, in the context of limited piped-service coverage and absent groundwater-permitting costs
parsed.outcome: Water-source access and use, service coverage, and household capital, operating, and maintenance expenditures indicating affordability
parsed.rationale: Section 2 (pp. 3–4) reports a questionnaire survey of 315 households and an identifiable life-cycle cost method. Sections 3.1–3.2 (pp. 4–8) empirically compare household access by water-service arrangement and associated expenditures, including self-supply adopted where public piped service was unavailable or unaffordable. The study also examines institutional and financing implications, including lack of formal recognition of self-supply, absence of groundwater-permit costs, and the need for government financing and support mechanisms (Introduction, pp. 2–3; Conclusion, pp. 8–9).
